source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Fall armyworm (ដង្គូវហ្គ្រង, Spodoptera frugiperda): the larva has a dark/blackish head, a body dotted with small round spots, and can grow to a length of roughly 30-35 mm. The larva has a body shape and coloring resembling grayish-brown/oat coloring. Adults live and mate for about 2-3 days after emergence before the female begins laying eggs; a female moth can lay egg masses of about 50 to 350 eggs in a single mass, and can lay a total of up to about 2,500 eggs over her lifetime. Moths lay eggs on the underside of leaves, in clusters, and eggs hatch within about 3-4 days.

Life cycle continued: egg hatching to pupation takes about 2-3 weeks. Larvae feed and cause damage particularly by boring into the whorl and growing point of the plant. After feeding, larvae drop to the soil to pupate, taking about 8-9 days, up to 15 days, before emerging as adult moths. Larvae feeding inside the whorl or growing point can kill the growing point when infestation is severe. In cases of severe infestation, this pest can cause significant loss of yield.

Prevention and control measures:
- Use resistant/tolerant varieties.
- Plant at an appropriate time.
- Remove weeds/host plants present in the field, especially around the field margins, and destroy alternate host plants that are related species.
- Collect egg masses and larvae and destroy them by burning.
- Use natural predators or biological/microbial control agents to help manage infestations.
